what_happened: Before handoff the ego was replaying the recorded human drive (0.0 m off the recording) and sped up from 4.3 to 5.7 m/s behind the white utility truck (actor 2) in its lane. The gap shrank to contact at exactly 4.7 s, the same moment the policy took over, so the front collision happened before the policy controlled anything. Because the replay hit the truck even though the human did not, the simulated truck is probably placed or timed differently from the real one.

The ego was still replaying the human log (0 m from it) when its front box began overlapping lead car 12 in the same lane. Collision_front is already 1 at 3.7 s, a full second before the policy took over at 4.7 s, so the failure is counted at the instant of handoff. This looks like an actor box or replay artifact (the ego is too close to or overlapping actor 12 in the recorded log), not a choice the policy made.

On the highway after handoff, the ego braked for no clear reason (17 to 10.7 m/s, with no lead vehicle close ahead) and drifted left over the lane line while car 1 was passing in the left lane. The ego's front hit car 1. The route command was RIGHT, and the recorded path went the other way. The hard braking probably also explains the later rear contact.

In slow highway traffic, the ego's front hit lead vehicle 5 in its own lane. The ego was going about 3.2–3.3 m/s and the gap (about 4–5 m, which looks like the distance between vehicle centres) had been shrinking since before handoff, while the ego was still replaying the human's path (0 m off the recording). The policy took over only 0.4 s before the collision and slowed only slightly (3.3 to 2.8 m/s), so it had almost no room to avoid a collision the replay had already set up.
